name: National Atomic Testing Museum
falloutLore: The Museum of Technology — what the pre-war world kept of its atomic ambitions. The whole thing made it into the Fallout universe as a monument to a civilization that split the atom and then split itself.
promptMessage: Your Pip-Boy is detecting an anomalous energy signature — a pre-war archive of atomic research, still intact. You're standing in the shadow of history, wanderer.
rewardMessage: The Atomic Museum's archive terminal spits out a commemorative holotag. CLASSIFIED ARTIFACT — ONE ISSUED PER VISITOR.

name: Trinity Site
falloutLore: Ground zero. July 16, 1945. The first nuclear detonation on Earth. The Fallout universe's entire existence branches from this exact latitude and longitude.
promptMessage: RADIATION SPIKE DETECTED. Your Geiger counter is screaming. The ground beneath you is still faintly hot — two centuries later, some things never cool down.
rewardMessage: You find a shard of trinitite — the green glass formed when the desert sand fused in the first nuclear fireball. There is nowhere else on Earth you could have found this.

name: The Greenbrier — Project Greek Island
falloutLore: A five-star resort built over a Congressional doomsday bunker. Decommissioned, revealed, and now open for tours. This is what Vault-Tec would have actually looked like if they'd been honest about it.
promptMessage: Vault construction detected in the surrounding rock. Your Pip-Boy is picking up old emergency broadcast loops on frequencies nobody uses anymore.
rewardMessage: A decommissioned vault access card — still embossed with a Congressional seal. It doesn't open anything anymore. That's the point.

name: Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station
falloutLore: A military command center carved into solid granite, designed to survive a nuclear strike. In the Fallout universe this is exactly the kind of place that kept broadcasting long after everyone else went quiet.
promptMessage: ENCRYPTED MILITARY BROADCAST DETECTED. Source: mountain installation, hardened against EMP. The signal is 200 years old and still strong. Whoever built this expected to outlast the war.
rewardMessage: A data tape recovered from a NORAD-adjacent terminal. Its contents have been classified for two hundred years and will remain so. The label reads: CONDITION ZEBRA.

name: Titan Missile Museum
falloutLore: A live Titan II ICBM still sits in its silo, one of the last in existence. The missile was deactivated but the silo survived. In the Fallout world, not every silo went dark.
promptMessage: LAUNCH FACILITY DETECTED. Silo structure confirmed, depth 3 meters. Missile status: UNKNOWN. Your Pip-Boy advises you to remain calm. Your Pip-Boy is wrong.
rewardMessage: A launch authorization key — one of a pair required to trigger a strike that never came. You only have one. That's the only comfort available.

name: Minuteman Missile National Historic Site
falloutLore: A preserved Cold War Minuteman missile silo, exactly as it was during the standoff. The bomb is still there. The launch codes are not.
promptMessage: SUBTERRANEAN STRUCTURE DETECTED. Nuclear launch facility, decommissioned — or so they say. Your Pip-Boy is logging coordinates whether you like it or not.
rewardMessage: A laminated operations manual — Launch Sequence Procedures, Minuteman III. Every page has been redacted except the last: IN THE EVENT OF LAUNCH, PRAY.

name: Los Alamos History Museum
falloutLore: The town built to build the bomb. In the Fallout universe, Los Alamos is where the Enclave's research division continued working on nuclear applications long after the war ended.
promptMessage: CLASSIFIED RESEARCH FACILITY — PRE-WAR DESIGNATION: SITE Y. Your Pip-Boy has flagged this location in fourteen separate government databases, all marked EYES ONLY.
rewardMessage: A reproduction Manhattan Project lapel pin — the kind scientists wore to identify themselves on site. Wearing this in the wasteland means something. You're not sure what.

name: B Reactor National Historic Landmark
falloutLore: The world's first full-scale nuclear production reactor. It produced the plutonium for the Trinity test and Fat Man. The entire American nuclear program traces back to this building.
promptMessage: REACTOR CORE SIGNATURE DETECTED. Graphite moderated, water cooled. Design obsolete. Legacy: incalculable. Your Geiger counter is registering historical significance.
rewardMessage: A decommissioned reactor fuel rod casing — empty, safe, and completely impossible to explain at airport security. Still warm to the touch. Probably just the sun.

name: Nevada National Security Site — Visitor Area
falloutLore: 928 nuclear tests, most of them above ground. The Nevada desert absorbed more nuclear yield than any other place on Earth. Mushroom clouds were visible from Las Vegas.
promptMessage: 928 DETONATIONS LOGGED AT THIS COORDINATE CLUSTER. Your Pip-Boy radiation counter has run out of display digits. Background reading: HISTORICAL.
rewardMessage: A radiation dosimeter badge from the Nevada Test Site — still registered to a name that has been classified for seventy years. It maxed out sometime in 1962.

name: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
falloutLore: The Smithsonian's collection includes Enola Gay and a full V-2 rocket. In the Fallout universe, the Smithsonian became a contested archive — Brotherhood of Steel wanted the tech, the NCR wanted the history.
promptMessage: PRE-WAR AEROSPACE ARCHIVE DETECTED. Brotherhood of Steel has flagged this location as a Priority-1 technology acquisition site. Arrive before they do.
rewardMessage: A Smithsonian Institution holotape — recorded pre-war, cataloguing exhibits that no longer exist. A docent's voice explains the Enola Gay with the calm of someone who doesn't know what came next.

name: National Museum of the United States Air Force
falloutLore: Home to actual nuclear delivery systems including B-29 Bockscar. The museum traces the lineage of every aircraft that ever carried a nuclear weapon.
promptMessage: NUCLEAR DELIVERY SYSTEM ARCHIVE DETECTED. Aircraft capable of carrying multi-megaton payloads, preserved and displayed. In the Fallout universe, some of these flew their final missions.
rewardMessage: A mission patch from the 509th Composite Group — the only WWII unit authorized to drop nuclear weapons. One patch per mission. This one has a date on the back that you recognize.

name: Bethesda Game Studios
falloutLore: The studio where Fallout 3, 4, and 76 were made. The people who designed the vaults, wrote the lore, and built the world you're playing in right now worked in this building.
promptMessage: VAULT-TEC CORPORATE HEADQUARTERS DETECTED. Pre-war designation: BETHESDA SOFTWORKS LLC. Source of Vault 77 operational protocols. Employee of the Month: Todd Howard.
rewardMessage: A Vault-Tec employee ID badge — DESIGN DIVISION. The photo slot is empty. The name reads: OVERSEER CANDIDATE. Welcome to the program.

name: Diablo Canyon Power Plant — Overlook
falloutLore: One of the US's last operating nuclear plants. Perched on the California coast, built on a fault line. In the Fallout universe this coastal reactor complex survived the war and became a key power source for the NCR.
promptMessage: ACTIVE REACTOR SIGNATURE DETECTED — civilian power generation, still online. In the wasteland, power means control. Someone is going to want this plant very badly.
rewardMessage: A nuclear plant contractor's dosimeter and access badge. VISITOR — ESCORTED ACCESS ONLY. Someone has crossed out 'escorted' and written 'good luck' in pen.

name: International UFO Museum & Research Center
falloutLore: Roswell. In the Fallout universe the 1947 crash was real — the aliens were the alien technology that the pre-war military-industrial complex reverse-engineered into plasma weapons, energy cells, and the REPCONN rocket systems.
promptMessage: ALIEN TECHNOLOGY SIGNATURE DETECTED. Your Pip-Boy model was not designed to process this reading. It's trying anyway. The display shows: TAKE NOTE.
rewardMessage: A fragment of metallic alloy recovered near Roswell — designation UNKNOWN, composition UNKNOWN, origin UNKNOWN. Your Pip-Boy cannot analyze it. Your Pip-Boy seems nervous about this.

name: Area 51 / Nevada Test and Training Range Boundary
falloutLore: Groom Lake. The classified installation the Enclave was based on in Fallout 2. Where reverse-engineered alien technology became the foundation of American military supremacy — and where some of it stayed buried when the bombs fell.
promptMessage: RESTRICTED AIRSPACE. DEADLY FORCE AUTHORIZED. Your Pip-Boy has been flagged by five separate automated defense systems. The Enclave sends its regards.
rewardMessage: An Enclave-era security chip — beyond-black clearance, single-use. The data stored on it has been corrupted beyond recovery. The encryption key alone would have taken a pre-war computer forty years to crack.
